analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/developer/test.md (lines 872-1742), with no patch hunks and no runtime code changes. The excerpts describe test procedures, not security behavior. I found no new attack surface and no threat-model assumption changed by this text.

The lines consistent with the canonical model are:
- Line 955: build-registry regressions are in the platform repo, and hardware smoke is optional rather than a per-release gate. This matches the T-054/A-017 text on official-build registration, and actual serving still requires live Apple proof and receipt verification.
- Lines 1047-1049: release qualification needs a Developer ID-signed provider, and ad-hoc signatures or green CI do not count. This is consistent with T-052/T-056.
- Line 930: the profile-inventory auth test uses pseudo-terminals and does not call real sudo or change profiles. This matches the foreground-terminal profile-inventory boundary.
- Lines 972-979: the Bedrock reviewer installs hash-locked dependencies in a trusted workflow, and live validation is separate.
- Lines 1063-1071: the Bonsai fixture uses a random key and root, does not touch Keychain or production cache data, and does not qualify signed persistence. This is consistent with T-041.
- Lines 1332-1337, 1647-1651, 1589-1592, 1604 and 1715 cover test isolation. Tests use disposable databases and cleared environments and send no production credentials.

Nothing here weakens TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011. The unchanged source files behind these tests (coordinator/internal/**, provider-swift/**) were not supplied, so I assessed no behavior beyond the text. The excerpt starts at line 872 and ends mid-sentence at line 1742, so the rest of the file was not examined. The next pass should confirm that no other files in the PR change runtime behavior.
